title: fix(plugin-gantt): an EMPTY host `data` array is "no host rows yet", not the rows (objectui#7333)
body:
Fixes #7333

Clause-②: no (copied from the claim): the gantt stops treating an empty host array as authoritative. It keeps fetching from the view's own source, as it does with no host array at all; no declared key, export or accept set moves.

## What changed

`ObjectGantt` read a host `data` prop at two sites, and both accepted `[]`:

- the short-circuit at the head of `reload` tested `data && Array.isArray(data)`. `[]` is truthy, so the chart adopted it and returned before its own query;
- the gating flag (`hasHostData`, a bare `Array.isArray(data)`) fed `recordQueryDerivesExpand`, so the same `[]` also switched off the object-schema gate and the data-invalidation subscription of the query the chart should still issue.

Both sites now read ONE predicate, `hostRows`, evaluated once per render: a host array counts only when it has rows. An empty one reads as "no host rows yet", and the chart reads from its own source exactly as it does with no host array at all. A non-empty host array is adopted as before.

`reload` reads the predicate through `hostRowsRef` instead of closing over `rest`. `reload` does not key on the host rows, so a closed-over value is the one from whichever render last rebuilt `reload`. When a host's rows arrive after an empty first render, `recordQueryDerivesExpand` flips and re-fires the fetch effect, and that run has to see the rows that flipped it. Ablation A3 below shows that the closure form gets this wrong. The `eslint-disable` reason on `reload`'s dependency list said `(rest as any).data intentionally untracked`, which is no longer true. It now names what it actually suppresses, `searchFields`, measured by linting the file with the directive stripped: base reports `rest` and `searchFields`, head reports `searchFields` only.

## Which gate, and why (objectui#7210 half 2, ruling a′, PR #7391)

The card left this open: gate on length, or on an explicit "the host owns the rows" signal. Its routing note said the length gate is enough if the wrapper does not forward host props. Ruling a′ lets a non-grid view fetch the whole filtered set up to a platform ceiling, and PR #7391 implemented it with the `object-gantt` renderer still forwarding nothing. Its "Not in this PR" section calls forwarding `data` "the explicitly fenced-off wrong fix". So no host owns a gantt's rows on the registry path, and none is planned. Adding a host-ownership signal would be a new prop contract with nothing pulling for it. **The length gate is therefore the one that matches the ruling.**

## Premise and reach (measured on `6cf599985`)

- **Both sites existed as the card and triage describe them.** Base run of the new pins: `Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5)`. Only the two controls pass.
- **Reach: no caller hands `ObjectGantt` a `data` prop today.** `ObjectGanttRenderer` (`index.tsx`) still destructures only `schema` and renders `ObjectGantt` with `schema` and `dataSource`, and `ObjectGantt.hostDataProp-7210.test.tsx` pins that. A tree-wide `git grep` for direct JSX uses of `ObjectGantt` outside tests turns up `index.tsx` and `demo/main.tsx`, both passing only `schema` and `dataSource`, plus the README and docs examples, which pass `schema`, `dataSource` and `onTaskClick`. `ObjectGanttProps` does not declare `data`, so a typed caller can only reach this through a cast or an untyped spread, which is how the existing tests do it. ⇒ **This hardens a published component's input. It does not fix a live defect.** The triage ruled it owed anyway.
- **`ListView`'s rows array for an api-provider gantt view:** `useState` starts it as `[]`, and the fetch effect's `ganttOwnsData` branch returns without writing it. So from mount it is exactly the `[]` this card is about. `ListView` withholds it from the chart, which is unchanged here.

## Surface note: two plugin-list comments corrected (outside the claimed file surface)

My change made two comments false, so I corrected them. Both are comment-only, with no code bytes changed:

- `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`, the `ganttOwnsData` block, said the chart short-circuits on `[]` and that forwarding would paint an EMPTY chart;
- `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.test.tsx`, the comment on the api-provider gantt `describe`, said the same.

Both now say that an empty host array no longer blanks the chart and that the withholding still guards against a non-empty array being adopted in place of the endpoint's rows. `ObjectGanttRenderer` and the `persistLayoutKey` comment are untouched, as the claim requires.

## Tests

New file `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.emptyHostData-7333.test.tsx`, five cases:

1. api provider + host `data: []`: the endpoint is read and its rows paint;
2. CONTROL, api provider + host rows: those rows paint and the endpoint is never read;
3. CONTROL, api provider + no host `data`: the endpoint is read;
4. host rows that arrive after an empty first render are adopted;
5. object provider + host `data: []`: ONE query, issued after the schema settles, already carrying `$expand` (this pins the gating-flag site).

**Ablation**, run once with a prediction written before each run. Mutations go through `ablation-replace` WRAP mode: the anchor hit once, the blob moved, the restore was proven against the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` was empty after each leg. Tests import `./ObjectGantt` relatively, so the resolution path is `src` and no build is involved.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | reload's site back to "any array" | 3 failed / 2 passed | `Tests 3 failed \| 2 passed (5)` |
| A2 | gating flag back to a bare `Array.isArray` | 2 failed / 3 passed (cases 4, 5) | `Tests 2 failed \| 3 passed (5)` |
| A3 | reload reads the closed-over `hostRows`, not the ref | 1 failed / 4 passed (case 4) | `Tests 1 failed \| 4 passed (5)` |

## Local gates, all at HEAD `404ea62`

- `vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-gantt/ packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.test.tsx`: `Test Files 83 passed (83)`, `Tests 764 passed (764)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. That is 82 plugin-gantt test files plus `ListView.test.tsx`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0`, after building the `@object-ui/plugin-gantt^...` closure (`Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total`). `--listFilesOnly` on the test program shows the new test file and 82 test files in it.
- plugin-list type-check was not re-run: the plugin-list diff is comment-only.
- `check-changeset-presence`: `✅ 4 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-changeset-no-major`: ✅.
- `check:changeset-claims` (report-only): 9 pending changesets name `ObjectGantt.tsx` or `ListView.tsx`. I read each paragraph, and none describes the host-data short-circuit.
- `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`: all OK.
- `check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the 5 paths: `✅ NOT GOVERNED`.
- **Lint, narrowed to the changed files and proven complete.**
  - Population: `pnpm lint` is each package's `eslint .`, and the root `lint:root` ignores `packages/*`. So the changed files are linted by the plugin-gantt and plugin-list configs.
  - Count: `eslint --format json` reports 2 + 2 files, 0 errors, 0 ignored.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off, and no local rule reads another file. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - `ObjectGantt.tsx` warnings went from 84 at base to 81 at head: `no-explicit-any` 75 to 71, and `react-hooks/refs` 2 to 3 (the render-time ref write, the same pattern as `effectiveDataSourceRef` and `reloadRef`).
- Repo-wide lint, the full test shards and the other `check:*` families are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- **Measured behaviour change in an edge case with no caller.** A direct caller that spreads `data: []` into a gantt with no record source and no `dataSource` now sees the chart's own error, "DataSource required for object/api providers", where base drew an empty chart. I measured this with a throwaway probe against both blobs and deleted the probe afterwards. It follows directly from the ruled semantics: the chart reads its own source, and here it has none. Once the host's rows arrive, the host branch adopts them and clears the error, as the adapter branch does. That last sentence is read from the code; I did not measure it for this no-source case.
- **Unchanged and still untracked:** a host swapping one NON-EMPTY array for another does not re-run the chart's load. The fetch effect keys on whether there are host rows, not on which rows they are. That was already the case before this change, and no caller exists. Carrier: none.
- `ListView.tsx`'s `ganttOwnsData` block still calls objectui#7210 half 2 "an open maintainer decision", and the `surfaceDrawsFetchedRows` block still says the gantt query "carries no `$top` at all". Both have been stale since PR #7391. I left them alone because they are outside this card. Carrier: none.
